_meta.title: Killings by law enforcement officers, by country (Wikipedia compilation)
_meta.what_it_measures: People killed by police and other state security forces in a year, as a count and as a rate per 10 million people (value = rate per 10 million, year = the year the row gives).
_meta.source: English Wikipedia, "List of countries with annual rates and counts for killings by law enforcement officers"
_meta.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 - Wikipedia text "available under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 License" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text_of_the_Creative_Commons_Attribution-ShareAlike_4.0_International_License). Share-alike: a derived data file must carry the same licence.
_meta.citation: Wikipedia contributors, "List of countries with annual rates and counts for killings by law enforcement officers", revision 1376855354, accessed 2026-10-22.
_meta.caution: This is a volunteer compilation of national sources of very uneven quality: government statistics, NGO counts, press tallies and academic studies, each with its own definition (police only vs all state forces, on-duty only, etc.) and year. Wikipedia itself flags the list as incomplete. Rows are not comparable as a strict ranking. Every row keeps the citations it gives; check them.
_meta.years: summary table 2012-2024 (one year per country); annual tables 1996-2025

fields.summary_table: the main table row: killings, police, military, intel_agencies, other, population, rate_per_10_million, year_listed, notes, citations (with cited URLs), raw cell text
fields.annual.<year>: count from the year-by-year tables, with any citation in that cell

notes: Rate per 10 million and population are as printed in the article (not recomputed).
England and Wales / Scotland / Northern Ireland, if listed separately, are keyed GB-EAW / GB-SCT / GB-NIR.
